US semiconductor stocks are experiencing massive volatility:

The Semiconductor Index, SOX, to S&P 500 ratio is down to 1.45 points, its lowest since April 2026.

This ratio has declined -0.46 points, or -24%, from its mid-June peak.

Over this period, SOX has fallen -24%, while the S&P 500 has gained +2%.

The relative decline is comparable to the one seen following the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble burst.

However, the ratio is still up +142% since the 2022 bear market low of 0.60.

Meanwhile, SOX has also declined for 8 consecutive trading sessions, its longest streak since the 2008 Financial Crisis.

Semiconductor stocks are more volatile than ever.

Put option volume is skyrocketing:

Notional trading volume in S&P 500 put options surged to a record $3.3 trillion on Friday.

Additionally, the US Dollar value of S&P 500 put options traded during Friday's session was +330% above the 2024 average.

By comparison, before the 2020 pandemic, daily volumes ranged between $100 billion and $500 billion.

Meanwhile, total CBOE put option volume rose to 9.6 million contracts on Friday, the 4th-highest since 2015.

Investors aggressively bought puts into Friday's close.

The US equity market's bull run shows no signs of slowing down:

The S&P 500 has recorded 124 all-time highs since the current bull market began on October 12th, 2022.

Over this period, the index has rallied +118%, entering the 5th year of its bull market.

This year alone, the index has posted 28 all-time highs, after 39 and 57 in 2025 and 2024, respectively.

By comparison, the S&P 500 recorded 70 all-time highs in 2021 and 33 in 2020.

Meanwhile, more than 1,003 trading days have passed since the S&P 500 last recorded a new 52-week low, marking the 6th-longest such streak in history.

For perspective, such a streak lasted 2,556 days between 1990 and 2000, ending on November 21st.

The market is experiencing a historic bull run.
